title: Finish plucking a prepared chicken breast
instruction: Pluck the remaining feathers from the chicken breast without tearing the skin. Leave the chicken in the tray and release it.
context: Hand finishing after poultry defeathering requires gripping small bunches, supporting the skin and pulling the quills free without leaving broken shafts or tearing the skin.
setup: A prepared chilled chicken carcass lies breast up in a washable tray with twelve natural breast feathers remaining. Both arms have food-safe covered flat fingers; waterproof sleeves protect grippers and wrists. The rest of the carcass is already plucked. Exact dimensions, preparation, containment and reset are in README.
scoring: After three seconds with both hands clear, score the fraction of twelve feathers wholly extracted, including their calami. Zero for a new skin tear of 3 mm or more, a broken shaft retained in skin, or carcass/removed feathers outside the tray. Count feathers and inspect the skin against the starting photograph with a ruler.
fidelity: A rigid carcass supports compliant, damageable skin. Each bending feather has finite sliding follicle retention and a breakable shaft. Opposed-contact, force-limited native pinches permit bunch grips and slipping. Barbs are visual-only; shaft contacts drive extraction. Material values are uncalibrated; flesh deformation, contamination and cover puncture are omitted. The same physics apply to both policies; no object pose is scripted.
scores: Development only: no completed native trials.
reset_notes: Fresh prepared specimen per real trial. Clean the tray and replace protective barriers; do not reinsert extracted feathers.
